R.4.8 / R.5.1 cutover bridge — converts a to/from the JS core-engine model (the { documentId, body: { blocks: [...] } } shape that coreEngine.createCoreEditor consumes). The hosted component (TmDocumentCoreEngineHost) sends to JS and rebuilds the document from on save. R.5.1 — full round-trip (no data loss on save). Round-trips paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, text runs + inline marks, paragraph alignment, AND the structural blocks that previously vanished: tables (rows/cells/spans/header + nested blocks, recursively), images (standalone ↔ a paragraph carrying a drawing run, plus inline ), and page breaks. Rich C# content the engine does not model (image source/asset/link/natural-size, token/field/note runs) is carried verbatim in a __docSource preserve channel and restored on the way back, with the engine-managed visible fields (text/url/size/wrap/position/caption/alt) overlaid on top so user edits survive.

members.description: The REGISTERED commands of decision G2 that are tablet-and-up: equations, the cell properties and comparing against sources. items.description: The document header of TmDocumentEditor (redesign DE-1.1): a document icon, a HeaderStart host slot, the title (and an optional subtitle), a version / template preview chip, the save state (Saving... / Unsaved changes / Last saved HH:mm:ss, one dot colour per state) and, on the right, the document actions: Search (opens the editor's find panel), Undo, Redo, Print preview, Print to PDF (rendered only when an export provider exists - G9: a built-in action exists only with the capability behind it) and the primary Save, followed by the HeaderActions host slot (Share and similar - the editor offers no Share of its own). Undo / Redo / Save keep the test ids document-undo / document-redo / document-save and the data-command values they had in the ribbon quick-access group, and render exactly once: here, or in the ribbon when TmDocumentEditor.ShowHeader is false. The header is its own inline-size container (tm-doc-editor-header): below 1024 px it drops the subtitle and the button labels (the accessible names stay), below 640 px it also drops the icon and the status text. items.description: The document editor ribbon: Home, Insert, Math, Layout, References, Review and View tabs (plus a contextual Header & Footer tab) and a quick-access save/undo/redo group when the header does not own them. Since DE-1.2 the ribbon is ONE icon row on the core TmToolbar (Overflow=Menu, Popover presentation): no group captions (a TmToolbarGroup is named for assistive technology and for its section in More), groups divided by vertical rules, icon buttons with a tooltip, and a visible label only on the primary calls to action (Link, Comment, Image, Table) in Ribbon mode. Which commands fit is measured by the core tm-toolbar.js; which ones leave is decided by priority (data-priority, declared in DocumentEditorBuiltInToolbar): Secondary before Primary, OverflowOnly commands (less frequent character formatting, paragraph spacing, the debug tools) only ever in the "More" menu, a role=menu with grouped sections, arrow keys and typeahead; a toggle is a menuitemcheckbox there. The text labels of Link, Comment, Image and Table give way first (Labels=ShrinkBeforeOverflow) before any command moves to More. The alignment is one item (the current alignment as its icon, a menu of four checked entries), the colour pickers, the image menu and the style gallery have a More form; only the table grid, the equation, symbol, page layout and header/footer popups stay pinned on the bar (they move onto TmOverlayPanel in a later phase).

items.description: The one frame of every floating editing surface of the document editor (redesign DE-1.4 .. DE-1.7): a thin wrapper over the core TmOverlayPanel with a header (title, optional kind line and icon, an X with a localized label), a body and an optional footer. A top-layer popover anchored to Anchor with no scrim, closed by Escape and by an outside press that is NOT swallowed (it still reaches its target), presented as the core bottom sheet on a mobile layout; it implements no sheet and no focus trap of its own. Pointer and click inside the frame are fenced so the canvas selection survives. Escape and the X raise OnClose and OnRestoreFocus so the editor can give the focus back to the canvas.

items.description: Shared header of a DocumentEditor inspector panel (redesign DE-2.1): an optional decorative icon, the title as a heading whose id the panel region labels itself by (aria-labelledby), an optional subtitle, a host actions slot and a close (X) button that appears only when OnClose is bound. The close button is named by the localized TmDocumentEditor_Close string. Panels of phases 5-7 adopt it; the form pattern it sits above is the .tm-document-inspector-form CSS pattern. The companion form pattern is CSS-only (_document-editor-panels.css): .tm-document-inspector-form with __section / __section-toggle (aria-expanded) / __chevron (TmIcon chevron-down, rotates), __section-body, __field (the label sits beside the control while the panel body is wide enough and wraps above it when it is not - an intrinsic flex-wrap, no container query; --stacked keeps it above at any width), __label, __control, __suffix (units) and __segmented / __segmented-option (icon or icon + text); --embedded drops the frame and the shadow for a panel hosted inside the inspector. A field keeps the implicit label-wraps-control association.

The entry is a button styled as a field: it raises OnSearch and the editor opens its find panel - the panel owns no search logic. The column folds into a rail (Collapsed / CollapsedChanged, aria-expanded on the toggle); the editor starts it folded while a desktop container is narrower than 1280 px (TmBreakpoints.Xl) so the page keeps its room, and the reader's choice wins over the width. A tablet or phone container does not render this component: there Outline and Pages stay tabs of the inspector panel (DocumentSidePanelTab.Outline / Pages, kept for compatibility; on a desktop container they lead to this column).
